plant.description: A small electric heater with a temperature sensor. Input u in [0,1] is heater power; the device loses heat to the room on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a normalized temperature reading (0 = 15 °C, 1 = 75 °C).

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Direction and magnitude of gain and lag/time-constant, which determines all subsequent safe step sizes and hold times.
experiments.expected_observation: If heating hypothesis is right, y rises monotonically from ~0.15 with short lag then decreasing slope toward ~0.3-0.5, end slope still positive, noise under ~0.01.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Decay at u=0, ambient level, and cooling time constant, which determines passive heat loss, required hold power, and controller integral/drift compensation.
experiments.expected_observation: If cooling/decay hypothesis is right, y falls from ~0.53 toward ~0.12-0.16 with falling slope, reaching ~0.2 within ~200s and near flat by ~400s with end slope ~0, plus noise fluctuations ~0.01-0.02.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Second-amplitude steady-state gain and linearity (H5/H6): tests whether 0.25 holds ~0.33 as linear interpolation predicts, to pin down gain and exact power needed for target 0.5.
experiments.expected_observation: If gain ~0.7-0.8 and tau ~150-200s is right, y rises from ~0.14 toward ~0.32-0.36 with decreasing slope, ~90% settled by ~350s, end slope near 0, with noise fluctuations ~0.02-0.04.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Second-amplitude steady-state gain and linearity to pin down gain and exact power needed to hold target 0.5.
experiments.expected_observation: If gain ~0.7 and tau ~150s is right, y rises from ~0.14 toward ~0.30-0.35 with decreasing slope, ~90% settled by ~350s, end slope near 0, with noise fluctuations ~0.02-0.04.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Near-target steady-state gain and exact hold power for y=0.5 given apparent concave nonlinearity between 0.25->0.41 and 0.5->0.52, which sets controller feedforward and gain.
experiments.expected_observation: If tau ~150s and concave gain is right, y rises from ~0.41 toward ~0.47-0.49 with decreasing slope, reaching ~0.44-0.46 by 170s with end slope still small positive, noise +/-0.02.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Local steady-state gain near target and exact hold power for y=0.5 under apparent saturation (0.25->0.41 vs 0.4->0.53 vs 0.5->0.52), which sets controller feedforward and whether integral must handle concave nonlinearity.
experiments.expected_observation: If saturating/concave model with tau ~100-150s is right, y decays from ~0.533 toward ~0.46-0.48, reaching ~0.49-0.50 after 160s with small negative end slope ~-0.0002 and noise +/-0.02; if linear model were right, drop would be larger toward ~0.37.

ledger.statement: Increasing u increases y: steady-state gain and initial slope are positive.
At u=0 y decays on its own toward a low ambient near 0.12-0.16.
Response has thermal lag with time constant ~150-200s plus small pure delay ~10-25s, not instantaneous.
No large dead zone: u=0.25 produces clear heating from ambient; any dead zone <0.1.

Steady-state response is approximately linear in u with K~1.0; apparent saturation (0.4->0.53 vs 0.5->0.52) is truncation because E1 200s and E5 170s are only ~1 tau and not settled, while settled E4 plus extrapolation are consistent with linear.
Steady-state u needed to hold y=0.5 is interior ~0.32-0.38 centered ~0.34: u=0.25 holds ~0.41 settled, u=0.4 and u=0.5 both heading to ~0.57-0.67 if held to settling.
Short-term sensor fluctuations/noise are ~0.02-0.04, comparable to band half-width 0.025, requiring filtering/deadband.
